correctness.rationale: The central degree-ratio stratification is correct: u=2 forces (r,s)=(2h,h), so summing the split-product curve bound loses only L^5 rather than L^6 and gives raw exponent 1/2+5 theta; u>=3 contributes 1/3+6 theta. At theta=1/20 this reproduces raw exponent 3/4 and, through Sneiderman's length-sensitive all-equal summation, short-gap mass exponent 13/16. The record needs repair because its claim that 2/43 is the limiting current short-interval input is obsolete: Runbo Li's newer Primes in almost all short intervals III proves exponent 1/24 with O(X(log X)^-B) exceptions. Re-running the same parameterized argument for theta>1/24 gives limiting short-gap exponent 439/576, with all competing forest branches still strictly smaller.

originality.rationale: Chojecki's source and Sneiderman's pinned reconstruction retain the cruder raw exponent 4/5; the latter's 43/50 refinement comes from length-sensitive equal-chain summation, not the reduced-degree-ratio stratification. The inspected Kielhorn Lean supplement uses a different connector-region construction and a much larger fixed theta; the main Kielhorn manuscript itself was not obtained, so that remains a stated residual risk. No searched source matched the 3/4/13/16 structural refinement or its updated 439/576 consequence.

scientific_value.rationale: The structural one-parameter worst case is a real quantitative improvement to the canonical prime-gap deletion analysis. Updating the analytic input strengthens the limiting short-gap exponent from the stale 2927/3698 to 439/576 while preserving the fixed theta=1/20 theorem and the all-fixed-logarithmic complement bound.
